mappings.note: Japanese fan: each colour band is a sector of a stated angle taken over an annulus, so (pi*theta/360)(R^2 - r^2) needs the sector formula and the two-circle composite together
areas swept by the minute hand in 14 minutes and the hour hand in 10 minutes; the clock-hand sweep named in C-7.3-LO-1, with elapsed time converted to angle
eight cushions of two sizes with a 5 cm allowance, areas summed and doubled for both faces; combined circles, no angle and no perimeter
given the pool AREA, recover the radius and then the CIRCUMFERENCE to count edge tiles; the item exists to make the student move between the two
nine small cakes versus one large: areas of several circles summed and compared, the same area-additivity family as the two-circle items
wooden edge = four rectangles plus four quarter-circle corners that make one whole circle; circular parts assembled with a polygon frame
detector field is a fixed sector; the item inverts A = pi*r^2*theta/360 for theta and then for r. Nothing rotates, so LO-1 rather than the swept-area outcome
perimeter of three circles whose diameters lie end to end along AB; circumference additivity, the perimeter side
roller: rolled length is an arc, so the angle turned and the length pressed both come from the arc-length formula; no area is asked for
windshield wiper, the literal example in C-7.3-LO-1; the blade covers only the outer 42 cm of a 63 cm arm, so the cleaned region is a 110 degree annular sector and the composite is real
hoist drum: the beam rises by the arc wound on the drum, so the angle follows from arc length; a length question, not a swept area
voltmeter pointer travels 5.5 cm along the scale; arc length solved for the angle
winch cable length to angle and back again; the arc-length relation both ways, with no area in the item
sprinkler that ROTATES through 80 degrees and waters a sector; a rotating arm sweeping an area, unlike the static motion detector which stayed at LO-1
pulley turned through 102 degrees raises the weight by that arc length; length, not area
barn roof: the curved width is an arc (LO-1), the cross section is a rectangle plus the segment under the roof arc (LO-2 for the segment, LO-3 for assembling it with the rectangle)
paddle wheel rolling with the current: distance per minute is circumference times revolutions, a perimeter quantity, matching the tractor-wheel item
stadium: circle less a right triangle and a square built on the radius; a circle-and-polygon composite, with no angle other than the right angles the polygons supply
rubble fills the minor SEGMENT cut off by the road surface AB; sector minus triangle is the whole computation, so LO-2 and not the general composite
